newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean '97 semiconductor exports seen falling.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean '97 semiconductor exports seen falling.

text.p: The Korea Semiconductor Industry Association on Wednesday forecast this year's semiconductor exports, excluding the assembly sector, would fall 9.1 percent to $10 billion from an estimated $11 billion in 1996.
The association said in a report that the nation's memory chip exports were expected to fall by 10.2 percent to $8.8 billion in 1997 from an estimated $9.8 billion in 1996.
Exports of non-memory chips, such as application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), are forecast to remain flat at $1.2 billion, it said.

The report said its forecast was compared to a projection by another trade group, the Electronic Industries Association of Korea, for all-sector semiconductor exports at $18.6 billion in 1997 versus an estimated $17.86 billion in 1996.
The association predicted the global memory chip industry's slump, highlighted by plunges in world prices due to oversupply, would continue until the end of this year before picking up.

The price of the most widely used 16-megabit dynamic random access memory (DRAM) is expected to fall to around $6.0 per unit this year, following a plunge to $8.0 in the fourth quarter of 1996 from around $34 in the first quarter, the report said.
However, South Korea's share on the global DRAM market is forecast to continue to rise to 40.3 percent this year from 37.6 percent in 1996 and 32.6 percent in 1995, it added.
